clue.text: Parish district or Black Country settlement

definitions.meaning: in old English local government a large parish was split into smaller divisions, each with its own name
in apartheid South Africa, an urban area set aside for Black residents; the surface suggests the Black Country, the industrial West Midlands of England

explanation.surface: A local-history question about villages in the industrial West Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Country is the industrial area round Dudley and Wolverhampton in the English Midlands; here the words mean a settlement for Black people in apartheid South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a community unit: a subdivision of a large parish, and a segregated South African suburb.

clue.text: Some say sherbet is an enjoyable drink

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following words, here a run of them, give the answer

explanation.surface: People claiming that sherbet makes a pleasant beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'sherbeT IS AN Enjoyable'; 'say' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion is a kind of drink, often taken in place of tea.

clue.text: Collection made by canon in support of politician

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: a whip is the party official who keeps MPs in line
a round is a musical canon in which voices enter in turn

explanation.surface: A churchman giving money to back a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' looks like a clergyman but is the musical form; in a down answer 'in support of' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip-round is an informal gathering of money from a group, for a gift or cause.

clue.text: Disturbance observed initially in the circus ring

definitions.note: stands for the material strewn on it, the floor covering of the ring

indicators.note: says the word for observed comes at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: saw means observed
a dust, as in 'kick up a dust', is a commotion or row

explanation.surface: Someone noticing a commotion first breaking out in a big-top ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but only sets the order of the two words. 'The sawdust' is a stock phrase for the circus world.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood shavings are traditionally spread over the arena floor at a circus, so the material stands for the ring itself.

clue.text: Man, say, crossing end of street is a carpet-maker

indicators.note: the island word lies across, so it goes round, the other letter

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island

indicators.note: the final letter of the word street is taken

explanation.surface: A man walking over a street corner turns out to make rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man, say' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, so ISLE goes round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a coarse plant fibre used for cords and carpets, so it is a carpet material.

clue.text: A lot of detectives opening in court are sharp

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the words in and court is taken

explanation.surface: Police officers starting a court case prove to be keen-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of detectives' reads as many detectives but is A plus CID, a body of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic remarks are tart and cutting, the same as sharp ones.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp is seen about, getting thinner

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: A charlady seen around the place who is losing weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the 1940s BBC radio comedy ITMA, and her name became British slang for any office or household help.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Mopp is a byword for a charwoman, someone paid to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: American politician stifling one's religious belief

indicators.note: smothering something means wrapping round it, so the politician goes outside

parts.note: Dem is short for a Democrat in US politics
one is I and the 's is S

explanation.surface: A US politician who suppresses his own faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifling' signals one piece smothered inside the other; 'one's' gives two letters, I for one plus the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator God who does not intervene, so a religious creed.

clue.text: Came round about the line to the dairy

indicators.note: the letters of came go around the next piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning
RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: Someone came back along the railway to the milk farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the word came around the short word for about, making CREAME, before the railway abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamery is a place where butter and cheese are made, a dairy.

clue.text: Impulsive action of English made an impression at first

indicators.note: the second piece's word comes at the start, so it goes first

parts.note: stamped means pressed a mark into something

explanation.surface: An English person's rash act impressed people early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' looks like a first-letter pick but only puts STAMPED before E.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden rush of people or animals acting on impulse.

clue.text: Current way to conform to prevailing opinion?

definitions.text: Current way to conform to prevailing opinion?

parts.words: Current way to conform to prevailing opinion?
parts.note: read literally, moving through water in the same direction as the flow; figuratively, going along with what most people think

explanation.surface: Asking how to fit in with today's popular views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as present-day but also means a flow of water, and 'prevailing' fits winds and tides.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means following the majority view, as a swimmer goes with the flow of water.

clue.text: Railway workers take new route, abandoning old train

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain

indicators.note: a new version of the word means its letters rearranged
the letter for old is dropped from the word route

explanation.surface: Railwaymen take a different route, leaving an old train behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops O from ROUTE, and 'new' rearranges RUTE as TURE. 'train' looks like a railway noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture a child or talent is to rear and educate it, the same as to train.

clue.text: Carry musicians in car to motor way? It's the least we can do.

indicators.note: the car and motorway carry the musicians inside them

parts.note: a Mini is a small British car
M is short for motorway, as in the M1
MU is the Musicians' Union

explanation.surface: Driving a band along the motorway as a small favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry' signals the union sitting inside the car and motorway pair, just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the smallest acceptable amount, the least that will do.

clue.text: Nothing left over when it's divided in the store

definitions.text: Nothing left over when it's divided
definitions.meaning: a number that a smaller number goes into exactly, leaving no remainder
in Britain, a chain store with many branches

explanation.surface: Sharing out stock in a shop so nothing remains.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'multiple' is British usage for a chain of shops, such as a big high-street retailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve is a product of three, divisible with no remainder; a chain retailer is called a multiple shop.

clue.text: Rules of conduct given by business promoter to 19

parts.note: PRO is a public relations officer, who promotes a company
the answer at 19 down is an army officer, abbreviated Col

explanation.surface: A firm's publicist handing manners advice to an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' refers to the answer of 19 down, a rank abbreviated COL.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the formal code of correct behaviour, especially in diplomacy.

clue.text: A disputatious type on the river?

definitions.text: A disputatious type on the river?

parts.words: A disputatious type on the river?
parts.note: one reading is someone who argues, a quarrelsome person; the other is someone pulling oars in a boat

explanation.surface: Wondering if an argumentative person is out boating.
explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling covers someone who rows (rhymes with 'cows'), quarrels, and someone who rows (rhymes with 'goes') a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both an oarsman and, by the quarrelling sense of row, an arguer.

clue.text: Bird found up trees, perhaps, in a city

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word bottom to top

parts.note: a crow is a black bird

indicators.note: suggests the following letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A bird spotted high in trees somewhere in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CROW into WORC, and 'perhaps' rearranges TREES as ESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is a cathedral city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Divine being abandoned outside the entrance to Thebes

indicators.note: the wicked word goes on the outside of the next letter

parts.note: abandoned behaviour is shameless and immoral

indicators.note: the first letter of the city name is taken

explanation.surface: A god left outside the gates of an ancient Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as left behind but means depraved; 'outside' puts IMMORAL round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek gods were deathless beings, called the immortals.

clue.text: Given fish, half of them rejected wine

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: the last two of the four letters of them are taken

explanation.surface: Diners offered fish turning down half the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns CODEM round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux claret from the Médoc district of France.

clue.text: Soldier without escort entering pass

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, here the solitary word into the mountain pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
lone means alone, unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A soldier going through a mountain pass alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the solitary word going inside the mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, so a soldier by rank.

clue.text: One of those proposals made in written notes

definitions.meaning: an approach or opening offer made in negotiation or friendship
an orchestral piece played before an opera, set down in musical notation

explanation.surface: Advances put forward in written memos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like memos but means music.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is both an opening approach to someone and an orchestral introduction to an opera.

clue.text: Petty quarrel over some unspecified fabric

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble
any means some or other, whichever

explanation.surface: A squabble about some unnamed material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like 'about' but places TIFF above ANY in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany is a thin gauze or muslin material.

clue.text: Last of the duets revised by Chopin?

definitions.text: Last of the duets revised by Chopin?

indicators.note: the final letter of the word the is taken
the letters of duets are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Chopin reworking the final duet in a set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' signals rearranging the letters, which follow the final letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote famous piano études, study pieces, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Moor where article is hidden in centre of cavity

indicators.note: the article is tucked away inside the middle letters of the gap
the first and last letters of the word for cavity are removed

parts.note: a hollow is a cavity or empty space
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A moorland where something is buried in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like heath but is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice. 'centre of' leaves OLLO; 'is hidden in' puts THE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is described as a Moor, a North African.

clue.text: There may be a hitch in his travel arrangements

definitions.text: There may be a hitch in his travel arrangements

parts.words: There may be a hitch in his travel arrangements
parts.note: a hitch usually means a snag, but here it means a hitched lift from a passing driver, for someone travelling on foot

explanation.surface: A traveller whose plans might go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' reads as a problem, but walkers often hitchhike.
explanation.definitionFit: A walker on a long trip may hitchhike part of the way, thumbing lifts.

clue.text: Turn aside, failing to cross lake

indicators.note: the flaw word goes across, around, the letter for lake

parts.note: a defect is a failing or fault

explanation.surface: Veering away because one cannot get over a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' looks like a verb but is the noun; 'to cross' puts DEFECT round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect is to divert something from its course, making it veer off.

clue.text: Doctrine giving rise to claim to be virtuous

annotationWithheld.why: Doctrine giving rise to claim to be virtuous (5): reading upwards gives AM GOD, but 'claim to be virtuous' gives AM GOOD, not AM GOD, and no other parse gives the answer
annotationWithheld.clue: Doctrine giving rise to claim to be virtuous

clue.text: Often drank great brew -but it's not appreciated

indicators.note: a brew is a mixture, so the letters of the three words are stirred together

explanation.surface: Someone often drinks a fine beer, but nobody values it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' looks like beer but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken as given and never thanked for is unvalued, overlooked.

clue.text: Lofty way to replace a pound in money

indicators.note: the letters for way take the place of those for a pound

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money
L stands for a pound, from Latin libra
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A grand way to swap a pound coin for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lolly' is British slang for cash; RD goes in for one of its Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly manners are haughty, as if looking down from a height.

clue.text: American city detectives wearing partners' cords

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: the partners put on the detectives like clothes, enclosing them

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are partners at bridge
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

explanation.surface: Police in a US city wearing their colleagues' trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' are bridge partners North and South; 'wearing' signals that they enclose the London police.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord, worn round the neck or used on ships for fastening.
